translation_en: Muammal ibn Hisham Abu Hisham narrated to me; Ismail ibn Ibrahim narrated to us; Awf narrated to us; Abu Raja narrated to us; Samurah ibn Jundub, may Allah be pleased with him, narrated to us, saying: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, often said to his companions: “Has any of you had a dream?” Whoever Allah wished would then tell him his dream. One morning he said: “Last night two visitors came to me. They woke me and said: ‘Come with us.’ I went with them, and we came upon a man lying down while another stood over him holding a rock. He dropped the rock onto the man’s head, crushing it. The rock rolled away, and the man followed it and picked it up. Before he returned, the man’s head had become whole again. Then he came back and did to him what he had done the first time.” I said to them: “Glory be to Allah! Who are these two?” They said: “Come along.” We went on and came to a man lying on his back while another stood over him with an iron hook. He pulled one side of the man’s face apart from the corner of his mouth to the back of his head, his nostril to the back of his head, and his eye to the back of his head. Abu Raja sometimes said: “He split it.” Then he moved to the other side and did the same as he had done to the first side. He had not finished that side before it became whole again, and then he returned and did as he had done the first time. I said: “Glory be to Allah! Who are these two?” They said: “Come along.” We went on and came to something like an oven. I think he said: There was clamor and shouting inside it. We looked in and saw naked men and women. Flames came up to them from below, and when the flames reached them, they cried out. I said: “Who are these?” They said: “Come along, come along.” We went on and came to a river—I think he said it was red like blood. A man was swimming in it, and on the bank stood another man who had gathered many stones beside him. Whenever the swimmer had swum for a while, he came to the man with the stones, who opened his mouth and put a stone into it. The swimmer then went on swimming and returned to him; each time he returned, the man opened his mouth and fed him a stone. I said: “Who are these two?” They said: “Come along, come along.” We went on and came to a man with the ugliest appearance one could see. Near him was a fire that he was stoking, while running around it. I said: “Who is this?” They said: “Come along, come along.” We went on and came to a dark green garden with every kind of spring blossom. In its middle stood a very tall man, so tall that I could scarcely see his head in the sky, and around him were more children than I had ever seen. I said: “Who is this, and who are these?” They said: “Come along, come along.” We went on until we reached a vast garden, greater and more beautiful than any I had ever seen. They said to me: “Climb up into it.” We climbed until we came to a city built with bricks of gold and silver. We went to its gate and asked it to be opened; it was opened for us, and we entered. We were met by men, half of whose bodies were as handsome as one could see, and half as ugly as one could see. They said to them: “Go and plunge into that river.” There was a river running across the garden, its water pure white. They went and plunged into it, then returned to us with their ugliness gone and in the most beautiful form. They said to me: “This is the Garden of Eden, and that is your dwelling.” I raised my gaze and saw a palace like a white cloud. They said: “That is your dwelling.” I said: “May Allah bless you both; let me enter it.” They said: “Not now, but you will enter it.” I said: “I have seen wondrous things tonight. What were the things I saw?” They said: “We will tell you. The first man you came upon, whose head was crushed with a rock, is a man who learns the Quran and then abandons it, and who sleeps through the prescribed prayer. The man whose cheek, nostril, and eye were torn back to his head is a man who leaves his home in the morning and tells a lie that spreads to the horizons. The naked men and women inside something like an oven are adulterers and adulteresses. The man swimming in the river and being fed stones is one who consumed usury. The ugly man beside the fire, stoking it and running around it, is Malik, the keeper of Hell. The tall man in the garden is Abraham, peace be upon him. The children around him are every child who died upon the natural disposition.” Some Muslims asked: “Messenger of Allah, what about the children of polytheists?” The Messenger of Allah said: “And the children of polytheists.” He continued: “As for the people who were partly handsome and partly ugly, they were people who mixed a righteous deed with another that was bad; Allah pardoned them.”
